title: Panna Cotta
subtitle: Italian set cream pudding with raspberry coulis
excerpt: Silky Italian set cream, sweetened with vanilla and set with just enough gelatine to hold its shape, unmoulded and served with a sharp raspberry coulis.

recipe.sourceNotes: Panna cotta (cooked cream) is an Italian dessert from the Piedmont region of northern Italy. It is a set cream dessert, thickened with gelatine rather than eggs: the result is a much silkier, more delicate texture than a baked custard or blancmange. The name first appears in written records in the late nineteenth century, though the technique of setting cream with gelatine is older. In Italy it is typically served with berry coulis, caramel sauce, or a drizzle of honey. The critical variable is the amount of gelatine: too little and the cream will not set; too much and it becomes firm and rubbery. The ideal panna cotta holds its shape when unmoulded but trembles when moved.

recipeTools.notes: A small saucepan for the cream. Six 150 ml individual dariole moulds or ramekins.

content.text: Bloom the gelatine sheets in cold water for 5 minutes until they are completely soft and floppy before squeezing and adding them to the warm cream. Do not boil the cream after the gelatine is added or the setting power of the gelatine will be weakened. The panna cotta needs at least 4 hours to set, and is better after 8 hours or overnight. To unmould, dip the base of the mould briefly in hot water and invert onto a plate.

Soak the gelatine sheets in cold water for 5 minutes until completely soft. Heat the cream, milk, sugar, and vanilla in a saucepan over medium heat, stirring, until the sugar dissolves and the cream just begins to steam. Do not boil.

Squeeze the excess water from the gelatine and stir into the warm cream until completely dissolved. Strain through a fine sieve into a jug. Pour into 6 lightly oiled moulds or ramekins. Refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight until set.

Make the coulis: blend the raspberries with the icing sugar and lemon juice. Pass through a fine sieve to remove the seeds. To serve, dip the base of each mould in hot water for 5 seconds and invert onto a plate. Spoon the coulis around the base.
